chapter: Learning, lawn parties and band rivalries
title: Lawn parties and Buddy Bowling's six-piece bands
summary: Dawson describes backyard lawn parties with tarpaulins and lights, which paid well for bands like Buddy Bowling's.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: What about lawn parties? Did you play at lawn parties? We played lawn parties.

Sometimes it was great. Lawn parties and dances that, uh, on Sunday night like that had a great, uh, that was a great thing, lawn parties. You know, people would have, uh, in the backyard, they'd have, uh, tarpaulin on the, on the, on the ground. Some of them would put tarpaulin overhead to keep it when bad weather would come up, like a rain or something, protect it. And from the night air. And have all lights all around to keep it lit up in the yard, big yard, they had to have a big yard to have a lawn party. And there was plenty of money in that. Made enough money to play a band.

Yeah. Now, uh, now, uh, Buddy Bowling used to play all them, them kind of parties like that, you see. Uh, all them other six piece bands used to, gets them lawn parties at night. There's plenty of music, uh, money in that.
